biography: Tim Richmond, a name synonymous with flair and raw talent, burst onto the Stock USA Gen1 scene from humble beginnings. Raised in the heartland, his early years were defined by a relentless pursuit of speed, tearing up dirt tracks in a beat-up pickup truck he affectionately called 'The Mule.' He honed his skills on those unforgiving surfaces, developing an uncanny ability to feel the limits of grip. Richmond's breakout moment came at the 'Thunder Valley Showdown' in 1978, where, against all odds, he wrestled his underpowered machine to a stunning victory, outpacing seasoned veterans. His flamboyant style and devil-may-care attitude quickly made him a fan favorite, but also drew the ire of some traditionalists. Despite battling personal demons and facing adversity head-on, Richmond remains a formidable force, a true maverick in the Stock USA Gen1 world, constantly seeking to redefine the boundaries of speed and style.
drivingStyle: Richmond's driving style is as bold and unpredictable as his personality. He's an aggressive driver, known for late-braking maneuvers and daring passes that often leave spectators breathless. He possesses an almost preternatural ability to anticipate the movements of other cars, allowing him to thread the needle through seemingly impossible gaps. While his aggressive style sometimes leads to costly mistakes, it also makes him a threat to win on any track, at any time. He is known to push his car and tires to the absolute limit, often flirting with disaster but rarely backing down.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing feud stemming from a controversial collision at the 'Riverside Rumble' in '82, where Hamilton accused Richmond of reckless driving.

McMillan's rough and tumble tactics often resulted in damaged cars when racing against Richmond, leading to several post-race altercations and accusations of unsportsmanlike conduct.

quirks: Always wears a lucky pair of argyle socks under his racing suit.
Insists on having a specific brand of cherry cola before every race.
Tosses a silver dollar into the cockpit just before the green flag drops.
famousQuote: "Life's too short to drive slow and wear boring clothes."
careerHighlight: Winning the 'Daytona Showdown' in 1984 after starting from the back of the grid due to an engine change. He sliced through the field with a masterful display of car control, snatching the lead on the final lap.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 'Charlotte Classic' in 1986 due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potential championship victory.
